expl: Mahavira Swami was born at Kundagrama or Kundalpur (near Vaishali) around 599 B.C. His mother Trishala was the sister of Chetaka, the chief of the Licchavi republican state of Vaishali, and his father Siddhartha was the head of the confederation of the Jnatrika Kshatriyas. His elder brother was Nandivardhana. In some old editions of National Council of Educational Research and Training books, Mahavira’s birth year is mentioned as 540 B.C. On this basis, many other publishers also printed the same year in their books, creating confusion. The correct birth year of Mahavira is 599 B.C., because Mahavira belonged to a period earlier than Gautama Buddha. Gautama Buddha was born in 563 B.C. In the newer editions of National Council of Educational Research and Training, Mahavira’s birth year is now published as 599 B.C.

stem: The first disciple of Lord Mahavira was –
expl: Lord Mahavira was born in 599 B.C. to Siddhartha, a feudatory of the Kshatriya lineage. His wife’s name was Yashoda, and they had a daughter named Priyadarshana. That daughter was married to Jamali, who later became a follower of Mahavira Swami. He was Mahavira’s first disciple.

stem: The salvation place of Mahavira, the Propounder of Jain religion, is located at -:

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The place of salvation (nirvana) of Mahavira Swami—the real propounder of Jainism or the 24th Tirthankara—is located at Pavapuri. Pavapuri, situated in Nalanda district of Bihar, is a major pilgrimage site for Jains. Lord Mahavira gave up his body at Pavapuri in Bihar in 527 B.C., at the age of 72 years. In the given question, instead of “propounder of Jainism,” the wording “real propounder of Jainism” should be used, because as the propounder of Jainism, the name of Adinath or Rishabhdev is mentioned.

stem: Which of the following is the earliest holy book of Jainism?
expl: The “14 Purvas” (Purva) are the earliest Jain texts. During the time of the last Nanda king, Sambhuta Vijay and Bhadrabahu were the heads of the Sangha. Bhadrabahu was the last person who knew the 14 Purvas given by Mahavira.

stem: Triratna or Three Jewels, i.e., right knowledge, right faith and right action are related to which of the following?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In Jainism, three means are described as necessary for liberation—right knowledge (samyak Gyan), right faith (samyak darshan), and right conduct (samyak charitra). These three are collectively called “Triratna” in Jainism.

Makkhali Gosala was initially a disciple of Mahavira, but later, due to differences, he gave up Mahavira’s discipleship. Various sources mention Ajivika teachers named Nandavachchha and Kissankichcha, who were active even before Makkhaliputta Gosala. This implies that the Ajivika sect existed even before Gosala. Probably, it was Gosala who made this sect popular. Therefore, by tradition, he came to be regarded as the propounder of the Ajivika sect.

stem: Who was the chairman of the first Jain Sangiti convened in Pataliputra?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The first Jain Council (assembly) at Pataliputra was held in the 4th century B.C., and Sthulabhadra presided over it. In this council, the 12 Angas of Jainism were compiled.

stem: Who of the following kings was strongly inclined towards Jainism?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/ More than one of the above

expl: Kharavela, the Chedi-dynasty ruler of Kalinga, was one of the greatest emperors of ancient Indian history. An undated inscription of his has been found in the Hathigumpha (Elephant Cave) of the Udayagiri hill, located about three miles from Bhubaneswar in the state of Odisha (Orissa). This inscription is the main source for understanding the history of Kharavela. He had a strong inclination towards Jainism. The Hathigumpha inscription is in the Prakrit language.

stem: The place where Mahavira attained complete spiritual knowledge (Kaivalya) is -
expl: After 12 years of severe penance and spiritual practice, Mahavira Swami attained Kaivalya (perfect knowledge) under a sal tree on the bank of the Rijupalika River near Jrimbhikagrama. As a result, he came to be known as a “Kevalin”.
